title: Why Deep-Sea Fish Are Red | Why It Happens #8
simplified: Simplified model: colours are shown fading one after another with depth; in real water each fades gradually and the depths vary with how clear the water is.

hook_candidates.text: This fish is bright red. So how does red help it hide?
Watch this red fish sink. Its color is about to vanish.
Deep-sea animals are red to stay invisible.
You'd spot this fish anywhere. Except one place.
Paint a fish red. Now watch it disappear.

parts.text: So how does red help it hide?
At a thousand meters, sunlight runs out.
Water soaks up sunlight, color by color,
By one hundred meters, no red light is left.
Blue light reaches deepest, so blue would show.
In the last blue glow, red looks black,
Down here, red is the color of nothing.

sources: Water absorbs colours unevenly: 'Blue light penetrates best, green light is second, yellow light is third, followed by orange light and red light'; red is filtered first. NOAA Ocean Exploration, 'Why are so many deep-sea animals red in color?', https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/red-color.html
'At 100 meters, red light does not penetrate and, at this depth, a red fish is difficult, if not impossible to see.' NOAA Ocean Exploration, https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/red-color.html

Red animals look black at depth: 'Red light does not reach ocean depths, so deep-sea animals that are red actually appear black'; 'the fish appears blackish because there is no red light to reflect'. NOAA Ocean Exploration, https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/red-color.html ; 'animals that live in deep water and are red are essentially invisible', https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/animal-color.html

Sunlight runs out at about 1,000 m: sunlight zone 0-200 m, twilight zone 200-1,000 m, aphotic zone below 1,000 m where 'Sunlight does not penetrate'. NOAA Ocean Service, 'How far does light travel in the ocean?', https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/light_travel.html ; WHOI Ocean Zones, https://www.whoi.edu/know-your-ocean/ocean-topics/how-the-ocean-works/ocean-zones/

Blue penetrates deepest, so few midwater animals are blue: 'Since the color blue penetrates best in water, there simply are not that many blue animals' in the midwater. NOAA Ocean Exploration, https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/facts/animal-color.html

Simplified: the order and the 100 m / 1,000 m marks are from NOAA; the intermediate depths at which orange, yellow and green fade in the animation are illustrative only (no source gives them) and are not spoken.
